title: 'Neither Delhi nor Pindi': Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman's 7 November message
dek: The line comes as the BNP stages its first big rally since taking power, with the Ganges water treaty five weeks from expiry and no date set for Mr Rahman's visit to India.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has used his message for 7 November, a national holiday in Bangladesh, to declare that the country will take orders from no foreign capital. "Neither Delhi nor Pindi, nor any other country; Bangladesh comes first," he said in the message, published on Friday, according to reports. Pindi, short for Rawalpindi, is the seat of Pakistan's army.

The line comes as India and Bangladesh have five weeks left to agree on the future of the Ganges water-sharing treaty, which expires on 12 December, and with no date yet fixed for Mr Rahman's first visit to India as prime minister. His Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) is holding its first big street rally since taking office in February, in Dhaka on Saturday afternoon.

## What the leaders said

Bangladesh marks 7 November as National Revolution and Solidarity Day. It commemorates the 1975 uprising by soldiers that followed a counter-coup on 3 November and brought Ziaur Rahman, the BNP's founder and Mr Rahman's father, to power. Successive governments have marked the day very differently: the BNP celebrates it, while the Awami League, which governed from 2009 until Sheikh Hasina was ousted in August 2024, did not treat it as a holiday.

In his message, Mr Rahman said that in 1975 "the soldiers and people of Bangladesh united to thwart all conspiracies against the country's independence and sovereignty". He said the "defeated forces" of that time, in the name of the "Grand Alliance", had later "turned the country into a subservient state following a prolonged course of conspiracy". The Grand Alliance was the coalition led by the Awami League. The message did not name India, Ms Hasina or the Awami League, but referred to a "fascist regime" and "one-party authoritarian rule". The BNP has long accused the Hasina government of being too close to New Delhi.

President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, in his own message, said the day "remains an unforgettable day in our national life" and that "our beloved motherland was once again saved from the peril of becoming a subservient state". He also called for mutual respect and dialogue in resolving national problems.

## A show of strength in Dhaka

The BNP rally is due to begin at 3 pm Dhaka time (2.30 pm IST) outside the party's Naya Paltan office and end at Manik Mia Avenue, with Mr Rahman, who is also party chairman, leading it, according to reports. The party's programme runs from 5 to 11 November.

Reports describe a tense backdrop: friction with an opposition alliance of 11 parties, flash protests by activists of the banned Awami League, crude bomb explosions during some processions, and continuing unrest among garment workers. Ms Hasina, who has lived in India since August 2024 and has been sentenced to death in absentia by a Dhaka tribunal, has said she will return to Bangladesh in December. A BNP leader in Dhaka was quoted as saying that if she returns, "the people of the entire country will deal with her".

## Why it matters for India and Bengal

The Ganges treaty, signed in December 1996, sets out how the river's dry-season flow at the Farakka barrage in West Bengal's Murshidabad district is shared between the two countries. It expires on 12 December. On 3 November the Ministry of External Affairs said only that the Joint Rivers Commission was the forum for talks on shared rivers; no meeting has been announced. Bangladesh's water resources minister has said Dhaka wants a new or revised treaty with a guaranteed share before the deadline. Any new arrangement affects the water available to Kolkata port and to farms and towns downstream of Farakka.

India has invited Mr Rahman to visit, but no date has been set. Mr Rahman skipped the BRICS summit in New Delhi earlier this year despite an invitation, and Dhaka sent no representative.

## What happens next

Mr Rahman's speech at Saturday's rally will be watched in New Delhi for any mention of India or Ms Hasina. The BNP's week of events ends on 11 November. The Ganges treaty expires on 12 December unless the two governments agree on an extension or a replacement.
